{{Quote|It was done sometime this morning. When I arrived, her assistant came in to tell her I was present&hellip;and found her in this state.|Elyas Caran, reporting Cha Niathal's suicide to Natasi Daala|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
'''Elyas Caran''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Diplomat/Legends|emissary]] serving the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. In [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], Caran was sent to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]] to escort ex-[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Cha Niathal]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to stand trial for dereliction of duty during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. However, upon his arrival, it was discovered that Niathal had committed suicide. Caran reported Niathal's [[Death/Legends|death]] to Galactic Alliance [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]], who instructed him to bring Niathal to Coruscant for a [[Funeral of Cha Niathal|funeral]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>'This has been done with honor, without error, and by my choosing. Niathal out.'<nowiki></nowiki>|Elyas Caran, quoting Niathal's suicide note|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
[[File:Niathal.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Admiral Cha Niathal]]
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Elyas Caran served the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] as a [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomat]] during the [[Time/Legends|time]] following the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Backlash" /> In [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=7260#17384444|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=2008-10-02|time=10:48 AM}} dates the beginning of the [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series to [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]]. As ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]'', the fourth installment of the series, is dated to 43 ABY by ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', its events must take place in 43.5 ABY.</ref> Galactic Alliance [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]] decided to have the retired [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Cha Niathal]] put on trial for dereliction of duty during the Second Galactic Civil War, to prove to the public that the Galactic Alliance government was treating [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force|military]] officials the same way that they had treated the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], whom they had put on [[The Galactic Federation of Free Alliances versus Luke Skywalker|trial]] for the same reason. As such, Daala sent Caran to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]] to bring Niathal to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to stand trial.<ref name="Backlash" />

When Caran arrived on Mon Calamari to speak with Niathal and escort her to Coruscant, he was greeted by [[Cha Niathal's assistant|Niathal's assistant]]. The assistant went to inform Niathal of Caran's presence, only to find that the ex-Admiral was [[Death/Legends|dead]], having committed suicide. Caran then contacted Daala's [[Aide/Legends|aide]]&mdash;[[Wynn Dorvan]]&mdash;via a [[Holocomm/Legends|holocomm]] message, reporting that he had a priority message for Daala. After Dorvan brought the Chief of State to the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building's]] [[Senate Communications Center|comm center]] to view the transmission, Caran informed Daala of Niathal's suicide, reporting that the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] had run a [[Gas/Legends|gas]] line of [[carbon monoxide]] into her [[Water tank (habitat)|water tank]], killing herself painlessly. Caran revealed that she had left a suicide note, and Daala ordered that the emissary read it. He quoted the note by memory, and Daala then instructed Caran to bring Niathal's body to Coruscant for a [[Funeral of Cha Niathal|funeral]].<ref name="Backlash" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|What do you&hellip;want done?|Elyas Caran, to Natasi Daala, after Niathal's suicide|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
Elyas Caran was regretful of Niathal's suicide, and he showed sympathy to Daala when he reported Niathal's death to her. When ordered to read Niathal's suicide note, Caran was able to quote it from memory, after which he became rather reflective. Caran was slender and elegant in appearance, with refined features, age lines on his face, and hair that he [[Hair dye|dyed]] jet-[[Color/Legends|black]].<ref name="Backlash" />

==Equipment==
Caran wore [[Pearl/Legends|pearl]]-gray and blue [[Clothing/Legends|garments]] that were cut like a military dress uniform.<ref name="Backlash" />

==Behind the scenes==
Elyas Caran appeared in a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] in [[Aaron Allston]]'s [[2010]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]'', the fourth installment of the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series.<ref name="Backlash" />
